---
title: "Step 1. Score the impact"
description: "Score six impact dimensions. A Level 4 makes it Business Critical."
---

Do this in [Phase 1, engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd), with your
commissioner.

Score what happens if the analysis is wrong, and who is affected. Score it in the
[Analytical Assurance Decision Tool spreadsheet]({{< var decision-tool >}}), which describes each dimension at each level. Opening it needs an NHSBSA account with access to the Analytical Quality and Assurance site.

## What you do

- Score each of the six impact dimensions in the tool, from Level 1 to Level 4: decision, finance,
  customers, legal or compliance, public visibility and reach, and reputation.
- Score against the tool's description for each level, not the dimension's name.
- For finance, use the thresholds in the tool. It marks them as still to be confirmed, so check the
  figures in the version you open.
- Take the highest single score as your impact score.

Your impact score is one side of the matrix that gives your level.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-assurance-level-matrix.qmd >}}

## Keep Level 4 for a material consequence {#what-does-not-by-itself-justify-level-4}

Keep Level 4 for analysis that is Business Critical, as
[NHSBSA defines it](../08-business-critical/index.qmd). The tool says:

> "Publication status, Board consideration, Official Statistics designation, media interest,
> national visibility, FOI disclosure, ministerial interest or parliamentary scrutiny do not by
> themselves justify a Level 4 score."

Score those under public visibility and reach. A Level 4 on any dimension makes the work Business
Critical.

## Outputs of this step

Record these in the Specification:

- The score for each dimension, and your highest single score.
- The Business Critical answer, yes or no.

## What you do next

- [Score the likelihood](score-the-likelihood.qmd) at design, once the data and the method are
  settled.
- If an impact dimension scored 4, go to [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).
